name.text: Finding the mistake in a grouped quartile

questiontext.text:
Kamau estimated the [[if test="is(qk=1)"]]lower[[else]]upper[[/if]] quartile, \(Q_{ {@qk@} }\), of the masses, in kg (to the nearest kg), of \({@n@}\) goats sold at Kiunga market. His working has one mistake.

Mass (kg){@lo[1]@}–{@hi[1]@}{@lo[2]@}–{@hi[2]@}{@lo[3]@}–{@hi[3]@}{@lo[4]@}–{@hi[4]@}{@lo[5]@}–{@hi[5]@}{@lo[6]@}–{@hi[6]@}
Frequency (\(f\)){@f[1]@}{@f[2]@}{@f[3]@}{@f[4]@}{@f[5]@}{@f[6]@}
  1. \(n = {@n@}\)
  2. Position of \(Q_{ {@qk@} }\): [[if test="is(er=1)"]][[if test="is(qk=1)"]]\(({@n@} + 1) \div 4\)[[else]]\(3 \times ({@n@} + 1) \div 4\)[[/if]][[else]][[if test="is(qk=1)"]]\({@n@} \div 4\)[[else]]\(3 \times {@n@} \div 4\)[[/if]][[/if]] \(= {@posd@}\)
  3. The cumulative frequencies are {@cfstr@}, so \(Q_{ {@qk@} }\) is in the class {@lo[kq]@}–{@hi[kq]@}.
  4. \(L = {@Lsd@}\)
  5. \(CF = {@CFS@}\), \(F = {@Fq@}\), \(c = 10\)
  6. \(Q_{ {@qk@} } = {@Lsd@} + \dfrac{ {@posd@} - {@CFS@} }{ {@Fq@} } \times 10 \approx {@shownd@}\) kg

(a) Which step has the mistake?

[[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]] [[feedback:prt1]]

(b) Give the correct value of \(Q_{ {@qk@} }\), correct to 1 decimal place.

\(Q_{ {@qk@} } =\) [[input:ans2]] kg [[validation:ans2]] [[feedback:prt2]]

generalfeedback.text:
Check each value that goes into the formula \(Q_{ {@qk@} } = L + \dfrac{\text{position} - CF}{F} \times c\): for grouped data the position is \(n/4\) or \(3n/4\) with no \(+1\); \(L\) is the lower class boundary, because the masses are to the nearest kg; and \(CF\) is the cumulative frequency of the class before the quartile class.

[[if test="is(er=1)"]]

(a) The mistake is in Step 2. Kamau used \(n + 1\). For grouped data the position is [[if test="is(qk=1)"]]\({@n@} \div 4\)[[else]]\(3 \times {@n@} \div 4\)[[/if]] \(= {@exd(pos)@}\).

[[elif test="is(er=2)"]]

(a) The mistake is in Step 4. \({@lo[kq]@}\) is the lower class limit. The class {@lo[kq]@}–{@hi[kq]@} starts at the lower class boundary, \({@exd(Lq)@}\).

[[else]]

(a) The mistake is in Step 5. \({@cfq@}\) is the cumulative frequency up to the end of the quartile class. \(CF\) is the cumulative frequency before it, \({@CF@}\).

[[/if]]

(b) \[Q_{ {@qk@} } = {@exd(Lq)@} + \frac{ {@exd(pos)@} - {@CF@} }{ {@Fq@} } \times 10 \approx {@qd@}\text{ kg}\]

questiondescription.text:
Statistics II: finding the mistake in a grouped quartile calculation

Grade 12 CBE Core and Essential 3.1: Find the wrong step in a worked quartile of grouped data, and give the correct value.

Core and Essential

This question is original to this project and does not come from Cassell, D., Instone, S., Ling, J., Scruton, P. and Shilton, S., SMP AS/A2 Mathematics: Statistics 1 for Edexcel, Cambridge University Press, 2004.

feedbackvariables.text: ch: if is(ans1="s1") then 1 elseif is(ans1="s2") then 2 elseif is(ans1="s4") then 4 elseif is(ans1="s5") then 5 else 0;

truefeedback.text: Step 3 is right: \({@cfq@}\) is the first cumulative frequency to reach \({@posd@}\). Look at the numbers that go into the formula.
The arithmetic in Step 6 is right for the values Kamau used. One of those values is wrong.

falsefeedback.text:
[[if test="is(ch=1)"]]

Step 1 is right: the frequencies add to \({@n@}\). Check the values that go into the formula.

[[elif test="is(ch=2)"]]

Step 2 is right: for grouped data the position is [[if test="is(qk=1)"]]\(n/4\)[[else]]\(3n/4\)[[/if]], with no \(+1\), and that is what Kamau worked out. Check \(L\) and \(CF\).

[[elif test="is(ch=4)"]]

Step 4 is right: the masses are to the nearest kg, so the class {@lo[kq]@}–{@hi[kq]@} begins at the lower class boundary, \({@exd(Lq)@}\). Check the other values in the formula.

[[elif test="is(ch=5)"]]

Step 5 is right: \({@CF@}\) goats come before the class {@lo[kq]@}–{@hi[kq]@}, which holds \({@Fq@}\), and each class is \(10\) kg wide. Check the other values in the formula.

[[else]]

Check each value in the formula: the position (\(n/4\) or \(3n/4\) for grouped data), \(L\) (the lower class boundary) and \(CF\) (the cumulative frequency before the class).

[[/if]]

truefeedback.text: That is Kamau's answer, which contains the mistake. Correct the step you found and recalculate.

falsefeedback.text:
[[if test="inc"]]

Your answer is in the right class, {@lo[kq]@}–{@hi[kq]@}. Change only the value in the step with the mistake, then work through Step 6 again, to 1 decimal place.

[[else]]

Your answer, \({@ans2@}\), is not in the class {@lo[kq]@}–{@hi[kq]@}, which Step 3 correctly found for \(Q_{ {@qk@} }\). Change only the value in the step with the mistake, then work through Step 6 again.

[[/if]]
